entry.name: bitnot~
entry.digest: Bitwise inversion of a floating point signal
entry.description: Use the bitnot~ object to perform a bitwise inversion on an incoming floating-point signal as either raw 32-bit data or as an integer value. All bit values of are set to , and vice versa.

arguments.name: operational-mode
arguments.digest: Processing mode for floating signal/floating-point values
arguments.description: Specifies whether the floating-point signal or floating-point value will be processed as a raw 32-bit floating-point value or converted to an integer value for bit inversion. The modes of operation are listed below.0: Treat floating-point signal input as a raw 32-bit value (default).1: Convert the floating-point signal input to an integer value.

attributes.name: mode
attributes.digest: Processing mode for floating signal/floating-point values
attributes.description: Specifies whether the floating-point signal or floating-point value will be processed as a raw 32-bit floating-point value or converted to an integer value for bit inversion. The modes of operation are listed below.0 - Treat floating-point signal input as a raw 32-bit value (default).1 - Convert the floating-point signal input to an integer value.Note: If you convert the floating-point signal input to an int and then convert it back, the resulting floating-point value will retain only 24 bits of integer resolution.
